message.content:
Sure! To capture what’s currently displayed in Google Chrome you can either:

| Approach | What it does | Typical use‑case |
|----------|--------------|------------------|
| **Selenium + ChromeDriver** | Opens a new Chrome instance, loads a URL, and takes a screenshot of the page (full‑page or viewport). | Automated testing, scraping, or when you control the page load. |
| **pyautogui / Pillow** | Takes a screenshot of the whole screen (or a region) and crops to the Chrome window. | When you want to capture whatever is already open on the desktop. |
| **pywinauto + pygetwindow** | Finds the Chrome window on Windows, gets its coordinates, and captures that region. | When you need to target a specific window without re‑loading it. |
| **Chrome DevTools Protocol (pychrome)** | Connects to an existing Chrome instance via CDP and captures a screenshot. | When you want to capture a page that’s already open but don’t want to relaunch Chrome. |

Which one sounds most like what you’re after?  
(If you’re on macOS or Linux, let me know so I can adjust the instructions accordingly.)
